newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Bank of Mauritius sees 6.9 pct inflation in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Mauritius sees 6.9 pct inflation in Jan.

text.p: The Mauritian central bank said on Monday it estimated year-on-year inflation at the end of January was 6.9 percent.
The Bank of Mauritius added in a report that the real rate of interest on savings deposit fell to 1.03 percent at end-January from 1.30 percent in December.
It said the rate on savings deposits with commercial banks in January was 8.0 percent, unchanged from the preceding month.
The inflation rate for the year ending December 1996 was posted at 6.6 percent by the ministry of economic planning in early February.

In line with the increase in the inflation rate, the overall weighted yield (bank rate) of treasury bills auctions went up to 10.66 percent in January 1997 from 10.05 percent in December 1996, before easing to 10.58 percent in February.
"In February 1997, the bank rate remained stable varying between 10.57 percent and 10.59 percent as compared to the range of 10.41 - 10.76 percent in January 1997," the report said.

Treasury bills sold by the central bank in February 1997 totalled 3.07 billion rupees, down from 4.68 billion rupees a month earlier. The bank said in February, it received bids of 3.37 billion rupees for a total of 3.20 billion rupees of bills it put on tender during the month.
In January, the bank put on auction a total of 4.70 billion rupees of treasury bills and received bids amounting 5.62 billion rupees.
"Market preferences switched from the 364-day bills to the 91-day bills in February," the report said.

"Commercial banks continued to be the major participants in the primary bill market. Their transactions accounted for 67.3 percent of total bids received, down from 81.6 percent in the previous month," it added.
In the foreign exchange market, the central bank sold a total of $23.63 million to and purchased $5.80 million from commercial banks during market interventions in February.
More forex injections to commercial banks took place with Mauritius Sugar Syndicate tender sales of hard currencies totalling an equivalent of $4.84 million in February.

In January, the central bank sold $20.63 million to commercial banks during market interventions and made purchases totalling $7 million. The Mauritius Sugar Syndicate sold an equivalent of $4.32 million during its tender sales in January.
In February, the Mauritian rupee continued to strengthen, but marginally, against most currencies of the island's main trading partners except the dollar and the South African rand.

"Between January 1997 and February 1997, the rupee rose against the French franc (4.0 percent), Deutsche mark (3.9 percent), Japanese yen (4.0 percent), pound (2.0 percent), Swiss franc (4.1 percent) and ECU (4.0 percent)," the report said.
"However, the rupee depreciated vis-a-vis the South African rand (4.5 percent) and against the dollar (0.5 percent)."

Foreign exchange reserves at the central bank totalled 17.46 billion rupees at the end of February, representing 24.1 weeks of imports based on the island's import bills during the fiscal year 1995/96, the report said.
At the end of January, foreign exchange reserves at the central bank totalled 17.12 billion rupees, representing 23.6 weeks of imports.
